## Paper

Inequity aversion improves cooperation in intertemporal social dilemmas

## World

resource_island

## Institution

Redistribution, reputation, and social-preference reward modifications.

## Agent type

Deep MARL agents with modified incentives.

## Theoretical benchmark

Social-preference shaping can improve cooperation in intertemporal dilemmas.

## Learning setup

Sequential dilemmas with reward modifications for equity, reputation, or cooperation.

## Metrics

Cooperation/trade/contribution, welfare, inequality, sustainability, reward-accounting versus state changes.

## Main result

Agents that consider future consequences exhibit sustainable behavior and achieve high common rewards for the population; CFC-Excitor modules improve cooperation in intertemporal social dilemmas

## What they prove

Consideration of future consequences (CFC) is a successful trait in social dilemmas; CFC-Excitor modules improve cooperation in intertemporal social dilemmas

## What they only simulate

Sustainable use of CPRs without extra effort of fine-tuning; cooperation in different settings

## What they do NOT test

Fine-grained CFC behavior; real-world application of CFC-Excitor modules

## What we need to reproduce

When institutions change rewards, check whether they alter state behavior or only accounting.

## How our project differs

The paper studies social-preference shaping. The repo uses simpler redistribution/reputation/tax hooks and must classify state versus reward effects.

## Implementation obligations

State metrics and reward metrics side by side; inequality metric; contribution/trade metrics; effect classification.

## Metrics to compare in our repo

Resource Island and Public Goods welfare versus state-metric comparisons; tax_schedule_sweep outputs.

## Failure modes to audit

Reward shaping presented as cooperation when state variables do not move; no inequality metric; no baseline/no-tax comparison.

## Project code comparison

Compare Inequity aversion improves cooperation in intertemporal social dilemmas to redistribution, reputation, and tax outputs. The repo should be explicit about accounting-only effects.
